repos.recent_decisions: 14 of 287 RFCs carry a 'submitted' date on/after 2025-06-01 in the RFC index itself (docs/contribute/governance/rfcs/_rfcs.yaml, which records submitted/reviewed dates and authors per RFC), newest RFC-0288 ('git clone fuchsia'), submitted 2026-10-15 and reviewed 2026-11-03 — two days before this survey. Used the index instead of git log: GitHub mirrors nothing of Fuchsia, and the googlesource gitiles history view (+log) returned '403: Forbidden, Please sign in' for this instance even though the raw clone is public.
repos.notes: code_lines is a sampled estimate, not a byte-ratio guess: took the full HEAD tree listing via 'git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD' (free under a --filter=blob:none clone, since tree objects aren't filtered, only blob content is — no extra fetch needed), counted 52,688 files across the core implementation extensions (.rs .cc .h .go .c .fidl .py .s), then fetched a random sample of 30 of those files and measured their real line counts (wc -l): 8,767 lines / 30 files = 292.2 lines/file average. 52,688 x 292.2 ~= 15.4M lines; even if the true average were half the sampled one, it would still clear the 100k floor by 75x. Measured via a sparse clone (git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://fuchsia.googlesource.com/fuchsia, then sparse-checkout set docs) since there is no GitHub mirror to use gh against; final clone size 337M, well under the 3GB cap. Clearest pass of the four: an unambiguous, purpose-built decision-document corpus (formal RFCs) at more than double the raised floor, scattered across 287 files with the largest at 1.45% of the total, an OSI licence, and recency confirmed from the RFC index down to days before this survey.
